articles.title: GHSA: OliveTin: Unauthenticated DoS via OAuth2 State Memory Exhaustion (Unbounded Map Growth)
articles.summary:
## Summary

OliveTin's OAuth2 login handler stores per-login state in an in-memory map (`registeredStates`) that grows unboundedly. States are added on every `/oauth/login` request but are **never deleted or expired**. An unauthenticated attacker can send millions of requests to `/oauth/login` to fill the map with state entries, exhausting server memory and causing a denial of service.

articles.title: GHSA: swagger-typescript-api vulnerable to authorization-token exfiltration via spec `$ref`
articles.summary:
### Summary

When the developer supplies an `--authorizationToken` (commonly required to fetch a private spec behind authentication), `swagger-typescript-api` attaches that token to the `Authorization` header of **every** subsequent HTTP request it makes while resolving external `$ref` URLs in the spec — with **no same-origin check, no host allowlist, and no scope-down** for cross-origin requests.
